critique.student_view: The answer is basically the only sensible option — A, C and D are cartoonishly wrong, so I learn nothing about how marks are earned. Real SPM would make me compare two plausible balancing strategies or interpret a score/notation excerpt.
fixes: Replace the three weak distractors with plausible misconceptions: e.g. 'menyamakan kelantangan semua instrumen supaya adil', 'mengutamakan instrumen berdinamik lembut agar tidak tenggelam', 'menaikkan tempo iringan supaya melodi jelas'.
Add a short stimulus (score excerpt, dynamic markings p-f, or instrument range chart) so the student must analyse rather than recall the definition.
Reword the stem to a command word closer to SPM analysis: 'Berdasarkan situasi di atas, mengapakah...' or 'Apakah kesan jika...' so the KBAT 'Menganalisis' claim is defensible.

questions.subject: Pendidikan Muzik
questions.question: Apakah istilah yang tepat untuk bahagian berulang yang dinyanyikan selepas setiap bait dalam lagu tersebut?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Pendidikan Muzik 4531/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4-5)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stimulus is a thin wrapper around a pure terminology-recall item, and the English-in-brackets glossing (Verse/Chorus/Intro/Bridge) is not how Lembaga Peperiksaan writes BM options. Real SPM Muzik items tie terminology to an actual notated or audio stimulus, not a one-line scenario.
critique.student_view: This is just 'do I know the word korus' — the 90 BPM and 'Rasa Sayang' details do nothing, so it doesn't train me to read a stimulus for the clue. Also the bracketed English translations feel like a textbook glossary, not an exam paper.
fixes: Replace the prose scenario with an actual short score excerpt or lyric sheet showing bait + repeated refrain, and ask which labelled section (P/Q/R) is the korus — so the stimulus is load-bearing.
Drop the English glosses in options; use BM terms only (Rangkap/Bait, Korus/Refrein, Pengenalan, Jambatan) as SPM BM papers do, or keep one term consistently.
Raise the demand to at least Memahami/Aplikasi: e.g. ask why the repeated section is labelled korus rather than bait, or which section changes each stanza — matching the KBAT claim.

questions.subject: Pendidikan Muzik
questions.question: Berapa jumlah ketukan yang diwakili oleh tiga not tersebut?
flags: no recognisable SPM command word in the stem

critique.closest_spm_paper: Pendidikan Muzik 4531/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4)
critique.teacher_verdict: The content is in-scope (nilai not penuh/setengah/suku) but the item is pure recall dressed as 'Menganalisis', and the stem 'Dalam skor, terdapat tiga not berturutan' is vague filler rather than a real stimulus. Real SPM Muzik objective items usually anchor notation to a printed score excerpt or a named time signature, not a verbal description.
critique.student_view: This is just 4+2+1 in disguise — nothing to analyse, and 'berturutan dalam skor' tells me nothing I can use. The distractors are also weak: 6, 8, 9 are all near-misses that don't map to a specific misconception, so I learn nothing about where I'd actually slip.
fixes: Replace the verbal stem with an actual notated excerpt (or a named meter like 4/4) so students must read the notes, not recall values.
Rewrite distractors around real misconceptions (e.g. confusing not setengah with 2 ketukan in 4/4 vs 6/8, or counting the not penuh as 2 in cut time).
Drop the 'Menganalisis' KBAT label or raise the demand: ask for total ketukan in a given time signature with a dotted/tied note so it requires applying note values, not listing them.

questions.subject: Pendidikan Seni Visual
questions.question: Which approach is the student using when imitating the artwork?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Pendidikan Seni Visual 2611/1 Paper 1 (objective) — but note the real SPM PSV objective paper is in Bahasa Melayu, not English
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem is a long English narrative that reads like a textbook exercise, not an SPM PSV objective item, which in the real paper is a short Baku BM question with a compact stimulus. The concept (Pendekatan Mimesis) is in scope, but the wording and language do not match the actual paper.
critique.student_view: This feels like a worksheet question, not SPM — the real PSV paper is in BM and the stem would not spend four lines telling me the teacher's rationale. It also does not test whether I can distinguish mimesis from formalistik/kontekstual in a real artwork stimulus, so it would not teach me the discrimination the exam actually wants.
fixes: Rewrite the item in Bahasa Melayu Baku and shorten the stem to one or two sentences, e.g. 'Seorang pelajar meniru setiap sapuan berus dan warna sebuah lukisan asal. Apakah pendekatan yang digunakan?'
Replace the long explanatory stem with a small stimulus (e.g. a described artwork or a short quote) so the item tests application, not reading comprehension.
Make the distractors more plausible by using approaches that students commonly confuse (Formalistik, Kontekstual, Ekspresionisme) and ensure only one is defensible from the stimulus.

questions.subject: Pendidikan Seni Visual
questions.question: Which element of art is primarily used to differentiate the tree bark from the leaves?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Pendidikan Seni Visual 2611/1 Paper 1 objective (Seni Halus)
critique.teacher_verdict: The item is structurally close to a PSV Paper 1 objective question, but the English wording is not how SPM PSV items are phrased (real papers are in BM with Baku command words like 'Apakah elemen...'), and the stimulus is a thin description rather than a visual. The 'primarily' qualifier also invites ambiguity between texture and value that a real scheme would avoid.
critique.student_view: This reads like a translated textbook exercise, not a real PSV paper — real ones give me an image or a clearer scenario and ask in BM. The answer hinges on 'primarily', and the explanation just restates the stimulus, so it doesn't teach me how to eliminate value or form under exam pressure.
fixes: Rewrite in Bahasa Melayu Baku with an SPM command word, e.g. 'Apakah elemen seni yang paling ketara digunakan untuk membezakan kulit pokok daripada daun dalam lukisan arang tersebut?'
Replace the verbal stimulus with an actual charcoal drawing image (or a clearer described artwork) so the discrimination is visual, as in real PSV Paper 1 items.
Tighten distractors so only one is defensible: make 'Value' clearly about tonal contrast in the stimulus, or drop 'primarily' and add a second cue that isolates texture.

questions.subject: Pendidikan Seni Visual
questions.question: Which statement correctly identifies the critical approach the student is using and the step she performed last?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Pendidikan Seni Visual 2611/1 Paper 1 (objective) — Apresiasi Seni / Kritikan Seni
critique.teacher_verdict: The content is in-scope and the stem is a reasonable stimulus, but all four options share the same approach and differ only in the final step, so the item collapses into a single recall check of the Feldman sequence rather than a real discrimination task. Real SPM PSV objective items usually test one clear concept with distractors that reflect genuine misconceptions, not four near-identical stems.
critique.student_view: This is basically 'do I remember the order of Feldman's four steps?' — the stimulus is decoration, and I could answer without reading it. It doesn't teach me how SPM would actually test criticism, where the distractors would mix up approaches (e.g. formalistic vs. contextual) or mislabel a step with a plausible wrong term.
fixes: Make the distractors vary the approach as well as the step (e.g. 'formalistic approach, last step interpretation', 'Feldman approach, last step analysis') so the student must actually use the stimulus.

Shorten or sharpen the stem to a single command word consistent with SPM PSV objective style, e.g. 'Apakah langkah terakhir dalam pendekatan Feldman yang dilakukan oleh pelajar itu?' if the paper is in BM, or keep English but use 'Which step did the student perform last?'
Remove the redundant repeated phrase 'She is using the Feldman approach' from every option; instead put the approach in the stem or make only one option name the correct approach.

questions.subject: Pendidikan Seni Visual
questions.question: Apakah peranan utama lakaran perkembangan idea dalam folio reka bentuk industri berbanding lukisan unjuran dan lukisan perincian?

critique.closest_spm_paper: PSV 2611/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4 Reka Bentuk)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stimulus and option set are structurally sound for a PSV Paper 1 item, but the stem is over-engineered with a long comparative clause that SPM would rarely phrase this way. The 'peranan utama... berbanding' construction invites ambiguity between 'main role' and 'difference', which an examiner would tighten.
critique.student_view: The stem is doing too much work — 'berbanding lukisan unjuran dan lukisan perincian' makes me re-read to check whether I'm answering role or comparison. Option D is obviously filler ('pengalaman pereka... untuk apresiasi') and would never survive a real paper's distractor check.
fixes: Shorten the stem to a single clear command: 'Apakah peranan utama lakaran perkembangan idea dalam folio reka bentuk industri?' and let the options carry the contrast.

Replace option D with a plausible misconception, e.g. 'Menunjukkan pandangan ortografik produk yang telah selesai direka' — a real confusion students make between development sketches and projection drawings.
Trim the stimulus to two sentences; SPM stimuli are usually tighter and the 'sebelum model 3D dibina' detail is not needed to answer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solenoid 0.5 m long has 200 turns and carries a current of 2 A.
flags: no recognisable SPM command word in the stem

critique.closest_spm_paper: Physics 4531/2 Paper 2 Bahagian B/C structured item (or 4531/3 not applicable) - closest to a Paper 2 structured question
critique.teacher_verdict: The structure (state formula, calculate, predict-and-explain) is plausible as a Paper 2 structured item, but part (a) asking to 'state the formula' for 2 marks is a recall giveaway that SPM rarely rewards that heavily, and the whole item is a straight plug-in with no stimulus. Real SPM electromagnetism items usually embed the solenoid in a diagram or a device context and demand reasoning, not formula recitation.
critique.student_view: Part (a) giving 2 marks just to write B = μ0nI feels like free marks I'd never see on a real paper, and there's no diagram or situation so it reads like a textbook exercise. It doesn't teach me the SPM skill of extracting n = N/L from a described setup or explaining proportionality with a proper 'because' chain for the C3/C4 marks.
fixes: Replace part (a) with a stimulus: give a labelled solenoid diagram or a device (e.g. electromagnet/relay) and ask students to identify N, L and hence n, so the formula is applied not recited.
Reduce part (a) to 1 mark or fold it into (b); reallocate the freed mark to a reasoning sub-part (e.g. explain why the field is uniform inside and weak outside) to match SPM mark weighting.

Make part (c) a genuine C4/KBAT item: change a variable (e.g. insert an iron core or halve the length) and require a comparison with justification, using SPM command words like 'Explain why' / 'Compare', rather than a simple 'doubles so doubles'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the half‑life of the isotope (in minutes)?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Physics 4531/1 Paper 1 objective (Section A MCQ)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem and calculation are SPM-appropriate, but the options are not in ascending order and the key is placed at C, which is atypical for Lembaga Peperiksaan objective items. The 2.0 g mass is redundant and not used, which is a minor flaw but not fatal.
critique.student_view: The mass of 2.0 g is never used, which makes me wonder if I missed something. Also, the options are not in order and the correct answer is C, which feels like a deliberate trap rather than a real SPM item.
fixes: Remove the unused 2.0 g mass or incorporate it into a second part of the question.
Arrange options in ascending order: A. 5 min, B. 10 min, C. 20 min, D. 30 min.
Ensure the correct answer is not always in the same position; vary key placement across items.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Hukum Newton manakah yang paling tepat menjelaskan mengapa kereta itu terus bergerak ke hadapan walaupun brek telah dipijakkan?
flags: no recognisable SPM command word in the stem

critique.closest_spm_paper: Physics 4531/1 Paper 1 objective
critique.teacher_verdict: The item is structurally close to a Paper 1 MCQ but the stimulus is over-engineered and the wording 'paling tepat' plus the 0.2 s detail invites ambiguity rather than testing a clean concept. Real SPM would either test inertia directly or use a stimulus that genuinely requires applying the law, not a scenario where the answer is still pure recall.
critique.student_view: The 0.2 s 'brek belum signifikan' feels like a trick to force 'first law', but a real paper would not need that qualifier—if brakes are applied, the car decelerates and the first law still explains the passenger's forward lurch, not the car continuing. This teaches me to hunt for a keyword rather than understand the law.
fixes: Replace the stimulus with a standard SPM-style situation: a passenger lurching forward when the car brakes suddenly, or a car coasting with engine off, so the first law is the clean answer without the '0.2 s' qualifier.
Change 'paling tepat' to 'yang manakah' or 'apakah' to match SPM command words and remove the implication that multiple laws could apply.

Make distractors test common misconceptions (e.g., 'Hukum Newton kedua kerana ada daya brek', 'Hukum Newton ketiga kerana tayar menolak jalan') rather than including 'Hukum graviti universal' which is obviously out of scope.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What happens to the energy carried by the wave?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Physics 4531/1 Paper 1 objective
critique.teacher_verdict: The physics is correct and the E ∝ A² relationship is in the KSSM syllabus, but the stem is a bare textbook-recall setup with no stimulus (graph, diagram, or data) and the wording 'increases by a factor of 4' is not the register SPM uses. Real SPM Paper 1 would embed this in a situation or a table and ask for a comparison, not a straight substitution.
critique.student_view: This feels like a textbook exercise, not an SPM question — there is no diagram or data to interpret, and the answer is a one-step formula recall. It would not teach me to handle the stimulus-based items that actually appear, and the distractors are too easy to eliminate because 'factor of 4' is the only squared option.
fixes: Replace the bare stem with a stimulus: e.g. a table or graph of amplitude vs energy for a water wave, and ask students to deduce the relationship or predict the new energy value.
Reword the stem in SPM register: 'A wave of amplitude 0.5 m carries energy E. When the amplitude is increased to 1.0 m, the energy carried becomes' — and use SI unit J in the options.
Make distractors plausible misconceptions: E ∝ A (factor 2), E ∝ 1/A² (factor 1/4), and E unchanged, so the squared relationship is actually tested rather than given away by option length.

questions.subject: Prinsip Perakaunan
questions.question: Berapakah modal permulaan Rania?
flags: no recognisable SPM command word in the stem

critique.closest_spm_paper: Prinsip Perakaunan 3759/1 Paper 1 objective (Asas Perniagaan / modal permulaan)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem and key are syllabus-correct and the wording is Baku, but the item is a one-step recall of 'modal = aset pemilik' dressed as application. Real SPM Paper 1 would either test the same idea through a short t-account/penyata or make the distractors carry genuine misconceptions.
critique.student_view: I can get this by spotting that RM7,000 is a loan and adding the other two numbers — no real accounting thinking, and the options are too easy to eliminate by length/position. It would not teach me how SPM actually distinguishes modal from liabiliti in a scenario with drawings, untung, or aset/liabiliti totals.
fixes: Replace the plain 'add two contributions' stem with a mini stimulus that includes a liability and an owner's drawing or additional capital, so the student must compute modal akhir or distinguish modal permulaan from modal tambahan.

Rewrite distractors to reflect real misconceptions: RM25,000 (adding loan to capital), RM22,000 (loan + cash only), RM15,000 (cash only), and RM7,000 (loan treated as capital) — avoid options that are trivially eliminated by magnitude.

Add a second sub-question or convert to a two-mark structured item (e.g. 'Hitung modal permulaan dan nyatakan satu sebab pinjaman tidak dianggap modal') so the cognitive demand matches the 'Mengaplikasi' claim.

questions.subject: Prinsip Perakaunan
questions.question: Apakah kaedah yang paling sesuai untuk menilai prestasi pekerja secara objektif?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Prinsip Perakaunan 3759/1 Paper 1 objective (MCQ)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem is a bare recall question dressed with a token stimulus, and 'paling sesuai ... secara objektif' invites a subjective judgement rather than a defensible single key. Also, detailed appraisal methods (KPI, 360-degree) sit at the edge of KSSM Form 4 Pengurusan Sumber Manusia scope, which is more about recruitment, training and remuneration than appraisal technique taxonomy.
critique.student_view: All four options are grammatically parallel and roughly the same length, so nothing signals the key except my memory of 'KPI = objective' — that is recall, not analysis. The explanation just asserts the other three are 'subjective' without teaching me how the examiner awards the mark, so it would not help me score a KBAT item.
fixes: Replace the empty stimulus with real data (e.g. a short table of KPI targets vs actual output for two workers) and ask which worker's appraisal is objective, so the answer is derived from the stimulus.
Drop 'paling sesuai ... secara objektif' and use a Baku command word tied to the data, e.g. 'Berdasarkan maklumat di atas, nyatakan kaedah penilaian yang paling sesuai dan berikan satu sebab.'

Rewrite distractors as genuine misconceptions (e.g. 'menilai berdasarkan pendapat penyelia', 'menilai berdasarkan kerajinan hadir') rather than three valid appraisal methods, so only one is defensible.

questions.subject: Prinsip Perakaunan
questions.question: What is the total labour cost (Kos upah) for this project?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Prinsip Perakaunan 3756/1 Paper 1 objective (SPM Form 4-5 KSSM)
critique.teacher_verdict: The item is a straightforward arithmetic exercise with a single-step formula, not an SPM-style accounting problem that tests classification or application of concepts. The distractors are not plausible misconceptions and the wording is too textbook-simple.
critique.student_view: This feels like a primary-school math question, not an SPM Prinsip Perakaunan item; the options are just random numbers and I can't see how this tests accounting knowledge. It wouldn't teach me to handle real SPM questions where labour cost is part of a costing scenario with direct/indirect classification.
fixes: Embed the labour cost in a simple manufacturing account or costing scenario where students must identify direct vs indirect labour and calculate total prime cost.
Replace the distractors with plausible errors such as forgetting to multiply by number of workers, using 8 hours instead of daily wage, or miscalculating days.
Use SPM command words like 'Hitungkan' or 'Calculate' and present the stimulus in a table or short paragraph typical of SPM accounting questions.

questions.subject: Prinsip Perakaunan
questions.question: What is the total capital (Jumlah modal) required for this project?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Prinsip Perakaunan 3756/1 Paper 1 objective (Pengiraan kos/capital item)
critique.teacher_verdict: The arithmetic is fine and the one-mark calculation fits an objective item, but 'total capital (Jumlah modal)' is conceptually wrong — this is total cost, not capital, and SPM would not conflate the two. The mixed English/Bahasa Melayu parenthetical and chatty 'project to produce wooden chairs' framing are not how Lembaga Peperiksaan words a stimulus.
critique.student_view: Calling the sum of material, labour and overhead 'capital' would confuse me — capital is owner's equity, not cost, so I'd second-guess the key. The distractors are just wrong sums, not real misconceptions, so it doesn't train me to spot the classic error (e.g. forgetting overhead or double-counting labour).
fixes: Rename the quantity to 'total cost (jumlah kos)' or reframe as capital contributed to start the project, and keep terminology consistent in one language.
Replace distractors with misconception-based options: omitting overhead (RM 1,820), counting labour as 2×5×8 (RM 80) only, or 4 days overhead miscalculated.
Tighten the stimulus to SPM register: a short table of cost items with units, no narrative 'project to produce wooden chairs'.

questions.subject: Sains
questions.question: Seekor ikan berenang lebih dalam di dalam air. Bagaimana tekanan air terhadap ikan berubah?
flags: no recognisable SPM command word in the stem

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sains 1511/1 Paper 1 objective (Form 5 KSSM, Tekanan)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem and option D are clean, Baku and within KSSM Tekanan, so it could pass as a Paper 1 recall item. But it is straight recall of 'deeper = more pressure' with no stimulus, so the claimed Menganalisis level is not supported.
critique.student_view: This is a one-line recall question dressed up as KBAT; I answer it from memory without reading the options carefully. It does not train me to apply P = P₀ + ρgh to a data or diagram stimulus, which is what the real analysing items do.
fixes: Add a stimulus (e.g. a diagram of a fish at two depths with h values, or a graph of pressure vs depth) and ask for a comparison or prediction so the Menganalisis claim is earned.

Replace the weak distractor B ('bertambah dan berkurang secara berselang-seli') with a misconception-based option such as 'bertambah kerana suhu air berkurang dengan kedalaman' or one confusing pressure with force.
Tighten option C wording to a genuine misconception ('berkurang kerana berat ikan berkurang') and keep options parallel in length so the key is not guessable by length.

questions.subject: Sains
questions.question: Besi berkarat apabila terdedah kepada air dan oksigen. Mengapakah ini merupakan perubahan KIMIA dan bukan perubahan fizik?
flags: one option is >2x the median length (gives the key away)

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sains 1511/1 Paper 1 objective (Form 4 KSSM, Jirim dan Perubahannya)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem is a legitimate SPM-style stimulus and the key is scientifically correct, but option C is a giveaway because it is the only long, fully qualified option while A, B and D are short and obviously wrong. Real SPM distractors are closer in length and each should represent a genuine misconception.
critique.student_view: I can pick C without knowing any chemistry just because it is the longest and most detailed option, so this does not test whether I can distinguish chemical from physical change. The distractors are too weak to teach me how SPM penalises the common 'colour change = chemical change' and 'mass decreases' misconceptions.
fixes: Rewrite all four options to similar length and specificity, e.g. A: 'Warna besi berubah dan haba dibebaskan', B: 'Besi menjadi lebih ringan kerana air diserap', C: 'Bahan baharu terbentuk dan perubahan tidak boleh dibalikkan dengan mudah', D: 'Besi hanya berubah bentuk tetapi masih besi'.
Remove the parenthetical 'ferum(III) oksida' from the key option and place it in the stem or explanation so the key does not stand out by extra detail.

Replace option B with a more plausible misconception such as 'Kerana besi kehilangan jisim apabila bertindak balas dengan oksigen' to match the explanation's note that rusted iron actually gains mass.

questions.subject: Sains
questions.question: Gambar rajah menunjukkan Matahari (M), Bumi (B), dan Bulan (L) dalam satu garisan: M — L — B. Apakah fenomena yang berlaku?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sains 1511/1 Paper 1 objective (Form 5 KSSM, Astronomi)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem and diagram are fine for a Sains Paper 1 item, but 'Apakah fenomena yang berlaku?' is a straight recall question dressed up as analysis, and the distractors are not built on real misconceptions. Real SPM would force the candidate to interpret the alignment, not just name it.
critique.student_view: The answer is obvious the moment I see M-L-B, so it tests nothing beyond memorising the three arrangements. The distractors are weak — 'Bulan purnama tanpa gerhana' is a giveaway because it is longer and oddly phrased, and I learn nothing about why the other eclipse types are wrong.
fixes: Replace the stem with a stimulus that requires reasoning, e.g. 'Mengapakah gerhana matahari hanya dapat dilihat dari kawasan tertentu di permukaan Bumi?' or ask which observation distinguishes gerhana matahari from gerhana bulan.
Rewrite distractors as genuine misconceptions of equal length and register: 'Gerhana bulan penuh', 'Gerhana matahari separa', 'Bulan purnama', each plausible from a wrong arrangement reading.

Drop the KBAT 'Menganalisis' claim or upgrade the item to a comparison/prediction task (e.g. given the arrangement, predict what an observer at a stated location sees) so the cognitive label matches the demand.

questions.subject: Sains
questions.question: Sel darah merah dimasukkan ke dalam larutan garam pekat (hipertonik). Apakah yang berlaku kepada sel darah merah tersebut?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sains 1511/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4, Sel dan Organisasi Hidup)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem is a standard SPM-style application of osmosis to red blood cells, but the options are too transparent and the KBAT 'Menganalisis' claim is overstated for a single-step recall of crenation. Real SPM would embed this in a diagram or data stimulus and use tighter distractors.
critique.student_view: Option A is the only one that names the correct process and direction, so I can pick it without really analysing anything. It doesn't train me to distinguish between hypertonic/hypotonic effects or to read a stimulus, which is what SPM actually tests.
fixes: Replace the plain stem with a simple diagram or table showing solute concentration inside vs outside the cell, so students must infer tonicity before predicting the effect.
Make distractors more plausible: include 'sel mengecut kerana garam masuk ke dalam sel' and 'sel membengkak kerana air masuk melalui osmosis' to test common misconceptions.
Change the claimed KBAT level to 'Aplikasi' or 'Memahami' unless the item is upgraded to require analysis of a novel scenario (e.g., comparing two solutions).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Berdasarkan perbandingan kos dan hari cuti sakit dalam stimulus, mengapakah amalan mencuci tangan dengan sabun disifatkan sebagai 'mencegah lebih baik daripada merawat'?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Science 1511/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4, Microorganisms)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stimulus is a reasonable SPM-style data/comparison setup and the key is defensible, but the stem 'Berdasarkan perbandingan kos dan hari cuti sakit...' is a bit long-winded and the option A is conspicuously the longest and most complete, which is a classic giveaway. Real SPM Paper 1 items keep options closer in length and phrasing so the key is not identifiable by shape alone.
critique.student_view: Option A is obviously the answer because it is the only long, fully-qualified sentence — I would not even need the stimulus to pick it. It also does not really test 'aplikasi'; it just asks me to restate the slogan, so it would not train me to handle a genuine KBAT comparison item.
fixes: Shorten and balance all four options to similar length; make distractors equally detailed so length is not a cue.
Tighten the stem to a single Baku command, e.g. 'Mengapakah amalan mencuci tangan dengan sabun lebih baik daripada merawat penyakit bawaan makanan?'
Replace option B ('membunuh semua mikroorganisma serta-merta') with a subtler misconception, e.g. 'sabun hanya membuang kotoran tanpa menjejaskan mikroorganisma'.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Berdasarkan teks, manakah kenyataan yang paling tepat menggambarkan tujuan utama KSSM ASK?
flags: no recognisable SPM command word in the stem

critique.closest_spm_paper: none - not an SPM item type (ASK is PT3/Form 3; SPM Science 1511/2 does not examine KSSM ASK curriculum objectives)
critique.teacher_verdict: This is a curriculum-objective recall item about KSSM ASK, which is a PT3/Form 3 subject, not SPM Science; SPM would test a stimulus-based application of technology, not 'what is the aim of ASK'. The stem 'Berdasarkan teks' has no text, and the key is the longest, most detailed option.
critique.student_view: There is no 'teks' to base the answer on, and option A is obviously the longest and most textbook-sounding, so I would pick it without thinking. It does not teach me to read a stimulus or apply a concept, which is what SPM Science actually rewards.
fixes: Replace the ASK curriculum-objective stem with an SPM Science stimulus (e.g. a short scenario or data table on a technology in society) and ask a command-word question such as 'Terangkan mengapa...' or 'Nyatakan kesan...'.
Remove 'Berdasarkan teks' or supply an actual stimulus text; align the item to Form 4 Science KSSM 'Teknologi dalam Kehidupan' rather than ASK subject objectives.

Make all four options similar in length and plausibility, and ensure distractors reflect common misconceptions about technology (e.g. 'teknologi digital tidak memerlukan pemikiran komputasional') rather than obviously wrong statements like replacing Mathematics.

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the eventual fate of these two stars according to the nebula hypothesis?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Science 1511/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4, Stars and Galaxies)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem is a textbook recall question dressed as a stimulus; SPM would either ask a direct recall item without the nebula framing or use a data/HR-diagram stimulus to force application. The distractors are too obviously wrong (C and D are absurd), so the item tests elimination, not understanding.
critique.student_view: The 'same nebula' detail is a red herring that does nothing, and options C and D are so silly I can guess without knowing the fate of stars. It would not teach me how SPM rewards using mass to justify the endpoint.
fixes: Replace the stimulus with a simple HR diagram or a table of star masses and observed endpoints, and ask students to infer the pattern.
Make distractors plausible: e.g., 'both become neutron stars', 'massive star becomes white dwarf, low-mass becomes neutron star', 'fate depends on nebula temperature'.
Reword the question to use SPM command words: 'Based on the nebula hypothesis, explain why the two stars have different final stages.' (structured) or 'Which inference is correct?' (MCQ).

questions.subject: Science
questions.question: Which of the following skills is NOT listed among the special features of the Science Form 1 textbook?

critique.closest_spm_paper: none - not an SPM item type (textbook-metadata recall; no SPM Science paper tests 'what the textbook's feature list says')
critique.teacher_verdict: This is textbook-front-matter trivia, not Science content — SPM never asks candidates to recall a publisher's feature list, and the stem 'The textbook states...' is not a stimulus. It tests memory of a page layout, not any KSSM Science learning standard.
critique.student_view: I've never seen an SPM question ask what the textbook's own feature list contains — this is unlearnable from notes and teaches me nothing about scoring marks. The 'NOT listed' negative stem with a safety-procedure distractor is also a giveaway-by-topic, not a real misconception.
fixes: Replace with a genuine KSSM Form 4 Science objective item (e.g., scientific investigation steps, measuring instruments/precision, or manipulating variables) using a data/diagram stimulus.
If 21st-century skills must be assessed, embed them in a scenario (e.g., 'which skill is applied when a student...') rather than asking what the textbook lists.
Drop the 'NOT listed' negative stem and the textbook-metadata framing; use a stimulus-based stem with plausible science misconceptions as distractors.

questions.subject: Sejarah
questions.question: Discuss the importance of empire formation to the Malacca Sultanate from political and economic perspectives, and explain how the administration of these territories was structured. [10 marks]

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sejarah 1249/2 Bahagian B (struktur/esei), KSSM Form 5 Bab 5 'Malaysia Merdeka' — but the stimulus and framing are not how SPM Sejarah sets this topic
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem is a generic English-language 'based on the following information' blurb about the Malacca Sultanate, which is not how SPM Sejarah 1249/2 frames items — real items use a source/stimulus (petikan, gambar, carta) tied to the KSSM Bab and ask 'Nyatakan/Jelaskan/Huraikan' in Baku BM, with marks broken down per point. The 10-mark split (political + economic + administrative structure) is plausible in weight but the command wording and stimulus are off-standard.
critique.student_view: This reads like a textbook summary pasted into a question — the 'Based on the following information' line gives me nothing to extract, and the model answer just lists points without showing me how the examiner awards 1 mark per point or where 'any TWO' applies. I also can't tell if 'empire formation' is even the KSSM Bab 5 framing (Merdeka) or a Form 4 Malacca Sultanate topic — that mismatch would cost me in the exam.
fixes: Replace the generic blurb with a real SPM-style stimulus (short petikan or carta about Malacca's territories/tribute system) and phrase the question in Baku BM with SPM command words, e.g. 'Berdasarkan maklumat di atas, jelaskan kepentingan pembentukan empayar kepada Kesultanan Melayu Melaka dari sudut politik dan ekonomi. [6 markah]' plus 'Huraikan struktur pentadbiran wilayah takluk. [4 markah]'.

Align the topic to the actual KSSM Form 5 Bab 5 'Malaysia Merdeka' scope — if the intent is Malacca Sultanate, label it Form 4 Bab 1, not Form 5 Merdeka; otherwise rewrite around Merdeka (e.g. pembentukan Persekutuan Tanah Melayu) so syllabus precision is honest.

Show a mark scheme in SPM style: split 10 marks into explicit sub-marks (e.g. 3+3+4), indicate '1 markah per point, mana-mana dua', and complete the truncated conclusion so the model answer demonstrates full-mark structure.

questions.subject: Sejarah
questions.question: Berdasarkan maklumat di atas, apakah faktor utama yang dapat mempercepatkan pembangunan negara bangsa Malaysia?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sejarah 1249/1 Paper 1 objective (MCQ)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stimulus is a single GDP statistic that does not logically entail any of the four options, so the item is not a valid 'based on the information above' question; real SPM Sejarah MCQs use a source extract or statement set that the correct answer can be derived from. The stem also conflates 'pembangunan negara bangsa' (nation-building) with economic growth, which is a syllabus mismatch.
critique.student_view: I can't see how the 5.5% GDP line points to digital infrastructure rather than heavy industry or tax cuts — it feels like the answer was written first and the stimulus bolted on. This wouldn't teach me how SPM tests KBAT, because real analysing items make me compare or infer from the source, not guess which option the setter liked.
fixes: Replace the stimulus with a short extract or set of statements (e.g. RMKe-10 priorities on digital economy, infrastructure, and human capital) so the correct option is derivable from the source, not from outside recall.
Rewrite the stem to match the topic precisely: 'Apakah kesan pelaburan infrastruktur digital terhadap pembangunan negara bangsa?' or use a 'Mengapakah...' command word consistent with SPM Sejarah.

Make distractors plausible misconceptions tied to the stimulus (e.g. 'pengurangan cukai' as a fiscal measure, 'perbelanjaan ketenteraan' as security) and ensure only one is supported by the given information.

questions.subject: Sejarah
questions.question: Which statement best describes the impact of the House of Wisdom on the development of Islamic civilization?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sejarah 1249/1 Paper 1 (objective, KSSM Form 4)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stem and options are structurally fine for Paper 1, but the distractors are absurdly far-fetched (market, military academy, Qur'an school) so the key is guessable without knowing the content. SPM Sejarah MCQ distractors are usually plausible misconceptions drawn from the same topic, not obviously wrong roles.
critique.student_view: I can eliminate B, C and D in two seconds because no one would confuse the House of Wisdom with a spice market or army school, so this doesn't test whether I actually know the translation-and-preservation link. It also doesn't teach me how SPM hides the answer behind a near-miss distractor.
fixes: Replace the three weak distractors with plausible ones from the same topic, e.g. 'It was mainly a centre for compiling hadith and fiqh rulings', 'It focused on developing new military technology for the Abbasid caliphs', 'It served as a hospital and medical training centre only'.

Tighten the stem to SPM style: 'Apakah kesan utama penubuhan Baitul Hikmah terhadap perkembangan tamadun Islam?' or in English 'What was the main impact of the House of Wisdom on the development of Islamic civilisation?' — avoid 'best describes' which is more IGCSE than SPM.

If keeping the stimulus, make the question require using it (e.g. 'Based on the stimulus, why was Baghdad important...') rather than pure recall; otherwise drop the stimulus and treat it as a straight recall item, which is what the current demand actually is.

questions.subject: Sejarah
questions.question: Based on Zainal Abidin Abdul Wahid's interpretation, what was the defining feature of Malay nationalism during the Melaka Sultanate period?

critique.closest_spm_paper: Sejarah 1249/1 Paper 1 objective (KSSM Form 4)
critique.teacher_verdict: The stimulus is a historian's interpretation rather than the document/source extract SPM Sejarah normally uses, and the stem 'Based on Zainal Abidin Abdul Wahid's interpretation' is a name-recall cue that gives away the answer. Real SPM objective items test the fact through a source or a scenario, not by naming the scholar in the stem.
critique.student_view: Option A is the longest and the only one that echoes the stimulus wording ('Tanah Melayuan'), so I can pick it without knowing anything — that teaches me nothing about scoring. The other three options are generic nationalism phrases that don't even belong to the Melaka Sultanate, so it's a one-line giveaway.
fixes: Replace the named-scholar stem with a short source extract (e.g. a quotation about loyalty to the ruler and Tanah Melayu) and ask what feature of nationalism it reflects, so the scholar's name is not the cue.

Rewrite distractors as plausible period misconceptions (e.g. 'loyalty to the Sultan only, with no territorial concept', 'rejection of the ruler in favour of a people's sovereign state') rather than generic anti-colonial slogans.
Equalise option length and remove the verbatim 'Tanah Melayuan' phrase from only the key so the answer is not identifiable by wording or length.

Avoid contractions in formal writing: 'dont' → 'do not', 'cannot' is fine but 'can not' is not standard.

critique.teacher_verdict: 29/30 is too high for a 556-word karangan that likely has minor language errors and lacks the depth of a top script; a real SPM marker would award around 22-25/30. The feedback focuses on a single English word and generic advice, missing the need to evaluate isi, pengolahan, and bahasa holistically.
critique.student_view: This feedback doesn't tell me what specifically to improve in my content or language to reach the next band; it only nitpicks one word and gives vague suggestions. I need concrete examples of weak sentences and how to fix them to score higher.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 359-word karangan with only three shallow isi and thin huraian sits in the 'Sederhana' to low 'Baik' range, not comfortably at 22/30; SPM BM karangan is marked on isi (relevan, cukup, huraian), bahasa (kosa kata, tatabahasa, ejaan) and pengolahan (kesinambungan, penanda wacana), and the feedback never names these dimensions or gives a mark breakdown. The advice to add concrete examples is sound but generic, and the 'karangan model' comparison is not how a real marker frames it.
critique.student_view: It tells me to add specific examples, which is genuinely useful, but it never shows me how the 22 was split across isi/bahasa/pengolahan, so I cannot tell which dimension to fix to climb to the next band. The 'how it should look' outline is just a model answer, not a mark-scheme, so it will not teach me to score the marks.

critique.teacher_verdict: The script is short (265 words), repetitive, and uses informal language, which would likely place it in the lower band (C/D) rather than Baik. The feedback correctly identifies weaknesses but does not align with SPM marking dimensions (isi, bahasa, pengolahan) and overstates the script's strengths.
critique.student_view: The feedback points out some real issues like informal language and repetition, but it doesn't tell me exactly how many marks I lost for content, language, or organisation, so I can't target my revision. The 'how it should look' outline is too brief to be useful for scoring higher.

critique.teacher_verdict: The script is competent but not 'excellent': SPM directed writing rewards concise, well-organised content and accurate language, and this script is overlong with a redundant subject line and some awkward phrasing. A trained marker would likely award 13–15/20, not 18/20, because the length penalty and minor register issues pull it down from the top band.
critique.student_view: This feedback tells me to cut words and fix the subject line, but it doesn't show me how to reorganise my points to hit the top band or which specific phrases cost me marks. I'd still be unsure how to get from 15 to 18 in the real exam.

critique.teacher_verdict: The script is short (158 words) and has frequent language errors, so 14/20 is generous; a real SPM marker would likely award around 9-11/20. The feedback correctly identifies some errors but mislabels the rhetorical question and does not use SPM marking terminology (content, communicative achievement, organisation, language).
critique.student_view: The mark feels too high for a script with so many errors, and the feedback doesn't tell me exactly what to fix to gain marks. I need to know how to improve content development and language accuracy to move up a band.

critique.teacher_verdict: The script is very weak: short (145 words), repetitive, with frequent grammatical errors and underdeveloped content, so 10/20 is too generous. A real SPM marker would likely place it in the lower band (around 6-8/20) because it barely meets the content requirement and shows limited language control.
critique.student_view: The feedback points out real errors and gives some useful tips, but the mark is misleading—it suggests I'm near a pass when I'm actually far from it. To score higher in SPM, I need to know exactly which band descriptors I'm failing and how many marks each section (content, language, organisation) is worth.

critique.teacher_verdict: 27/30 is generous for a 276-word essay; SPM English 1119 continuous writing rewards length, range and mature vocabulary, and 276 words is on the short side for a top-band script, so a trained marker would more likely sit this in the 22-25 range. The feedback is sensible advice but is written in generic 'essay-improvement' language rather than SPM marking dimensions (content, communicative achievement, organisation, language), and it never mentions word count, which is the single most fixable gap here.
critique.student_view: The advice about adding a real concession and rebuttal is genuinely useful and I could apply it, but it doesn't tell me how SPM actually awards marks, so I can't tell whether 27 is real or inflated. Nothing here warns me that 276 words is short for a top-band script, which is the thing most likely to cost me marks in the real exam.

critique.teacher_verdict: 18/30 is generous for a script with frequent subject-verb agreement errors, limited vocabulary, and underdeveloped content; a real SPM marker would likely place this in the 13-16 range (Band C/D). The feedback correctly identifies some errors but uses vague terms like 'language accuracy' instead of SPM dimensions (content, communicative achievement, organisation, language) and does not quantify how many marks each improvement would gain.
critique.student_view: This feedback points out some real mistakes, but it doesn't tell me exactly what band I'm in or how many marks I'd gain by fixing each error, so it won't help me target the next band. The 'how it should look' outline is useful, but the mark of 18/30 feels inflated and could mislead me about my actual SPM standard.

critique.teacher_verdict: A 188-word script with frequent basic errors and undeveloped points would sit in the lower band (around 9-12/30), not 14/30. The feedback is directionally right but uses generic 'add a statistic' advice rather than SPM's content-language-organisation mark scheme.
critique.student_view: It tells me to add examples and fix grammar, but it doesn't show me how SPM examiners actually award marks for content, language and organisation, so I'd still be guessing what to change to jump a band.

critique.real_scheme: SPM 1103 Kertas 1 Bahagian B (Karangan Respons Terbuka) is marked holistically out of 30, but examiners apply an implicit two-part split: Isi (content) ~15 and Bahasa (language) ~15, then combine into a single band. Actual Lembaga Peperiksaan band descriptors (as commonly used in marking schemes/trial papers) are: Cemerlang 26-30; Baik 21-25 (some schemes split Baik 21-25 and Sederhana 16-20); Memuaskan 11-15; Kurang 1-10. Descriptors cover Isi (relevan, matang, huraian/contoh), Bahasa (gramatis, kosa kata, ejaan/tanda baca) and Pengolahan/Format. Under-length (<350 words) is penalised (typically a language/isi deduction, not automatic fail). Off-topic answers score very low or zero for isi.

discrepancies.app_says: 3 bands: Cemerlang 26-30, Baik 16-25, Memuaskan 1-15
discrepancies.real_spm: Typically 4 bands (Cemerlang/Baik/Sederhana/Memuaskan/Kurang depending on scheme); 'Baik' is usually 21-25, not 16-25
Baik normally ~21-25; 16-20 is Sederhana

discrepancies.app_says: Single holistic band, no isi/bahasa split
discrepancies.real_spm: Examiners mentally split Isi (~15) and Bahasa (~15) before banding

discrepancies.app_says: Only states min 350 words, no penalty rule
discrepancies.real_spm: Explicit deduction for under-length karangan

discrepancies.app_says: Not addressed
discrepancies.real_spm: Off-topic = isi marks near zero / very low band

discrepancies.app_says: Cemerlang/Baik/Memuaskan
discrepancies.real_spm: Usually includes Sederhana and Kurang

missing_in_app: Explicit isi vs bahasa mark allocation
Under-length (<350 words) penalty
Off-topic / luar tajuk penalty
Format marks for format-specific karangan (e.g. surat, laporan)
Deduction for copying stimulus text
Separate Sederhana and Kurang bands
Ejaan/tanda baca and kosa kata as distinct sub-criteria
critique.teacher_verdict: The 30-mark total and 350-word minimum are correct, but the band ranges are wrong: 'Baik' at 16-25 is far too wide and swallows the real Sederhana band. A real marker also applies isi/bahasa split, under-length and off-topic penalties, none of which the rubric captures.

critique.real_required_length: about 125–150 words (the instruction in the paper is 'In about 125 words' / 'Write between 125 and 150 words'; the CEFR-aligned 1119 directed writing task)
critique.real_scheme: SPM 1119 Paper 1 Part 2 (Directed Writing) is marked holistically out of 20 using three banded criteria, each contributing to the total: (1) Content — all/most/some of the given content points addressed and developed; (2) Communicative Achievement / Format & Register — correct text-type conventions (letter, email, article, report, review, speech) and appropriate tone/register for audience; (3) Language — range, accuracy, cohesion, and effect on the reader. In practice markers award a single band mark 1–20 (or the three sub-criteria are totalled), with bands commonly described as Excellent/Very good (approx 16–20), Good/Satisfactory (approx 11–15), Weak/Limited (approx 6–10), Very weak (1–5). Under-length (well below 125 words) and off-topic/ignoring the given points are penalised; content points not covered cap the Content criterion.

discrepancies.real_spm: Markers use holistic banding typically with four or more descriptive bands (Excellent/Good/Satisfactory/Weak) and the ranges are not fixed at 16–20/9–15/1–8; the B band in the app is unusually wide (9–15 = 7 marks) and lumps 'good' with 'barely satisfactory', which is not how SPM descriptors are graded

discrepancies.app_says: Single descriptor block per band covering content, format/register and language together
discrepancies.real_spm: Content, Communicative Achievement (format/register) and Language are separately weighted criteria that combine to the /20; the app collapses them so a candidate strong in language but missing points, or vice versa, cannot be scored the way a real marker would

discrepancies.item: Content points as a hard requirement
discrepancies.app_says: 'All content points addressed' for Band A only
discrepancies.real_spm: The task supplies a fixed set of content points (typically 4–5 bullets); markers check each one explicitly and uncovered points directly cap the content mark — the rubric gives no per-point mechanism or count

discrepancies.app_says: No penalty mentioned; only 'about 125–150 words' stated
discrepancies.real_spm: Writing substantially below the required length is penalised (content/language not given full credit); the rubric has no under-length rule, so a 60-word answer could still be banded on quality alone

discrepancies.app_says: Band C mentions 'weak or wrong format/register' but no explicit penalty
discrepancies.real_spm: Wrong text type (e.g. writing an article when asked for a letter) or off-topic writing is penalised and can cap the Communicative Achievement mark; app treats it only as a Band C trigger

discrepancies.app_says: 'about 125–150 words'
discrepancies.real_spm: The paper instructs 'in about 125 words' (some versions give a 125–150 range); presenting it as a strict 125–150 band is slightly off but broadly acceptable

missing_in_app: Explicit per-content-point checking with a count (e.g. 5 points, deduct per missing point)
Separate marks/weighting for Content vs Communicative Achievement (format & register) vs Language
Under-length penalty rule and how it is applied
Off-topic / wrong-text-type penalty and its effect on the format criterion
Register/audience specification per text type (formal letter vs informal email vs article)
Cohesion/linking and range as distinct from 'accuracy'
Spelling/punctuation tolerance and how serious errors affect the language mark
Guidance that the mark is holistic — a single best-fit band, not averaged sub-scores
critique.teacher_verdict: The 20-mark total and ~125-word length are right, but the three-band A/B/C structure with those fixed ranges does not match how SPM 1119 directed writing is actually marked — real markers use separate Content, Communicative Achievement and Language criteria combined holistically, with explicit under-length and off-topic penalties. As written, this rubric would let a marker award 16–20 for fluent writing that ignores half the content points, which no SPM examiner would do.

critique.real_required_length: At least 200 words for Part 3 (Continuous Writing); the paper does not specify 250 words as a minimum — 200 words is the working threshold
critique.real_scheme: SPM 1119 (KSSM, English 1119) Paper 1 Part 3 Continuous Writing is worth 30 marks, assessed on THREE marking criteria each out of 10: (1) Content/Ideas (relevance, development, support) 10 marks; (2) Language/Accuracy (vocabulary, sentence structures, grammar, spelling, punctuation) 10 marks; (3) Organisation/Communicative Achievement — paragraphing, coherence, cohesion, register and genre/task conventions — 10 marks. In practice examiners award a band per criterion rather than a single holistic band. The older CEFR-aligned band descriptors (Band A/B/C or 'Excellent/Good/Satisfactory/Weak') are applied per criterion, not as one overall A/B/C band spanning 25-30 / 14-24 / 1-13.

discrepancies.app_says: One holistic band (A 25-30, B 14-24, C 1-13) applied to the whole essay
discrepancies.real_spm: Three separate criteria (Content, Language, Organisation/Communicative Achievement) each out of 10, banded independently, then totalled

discrepancies.app_says: A=25-30, B=14-24, C=1-13 (three bands only)
discrepancies.real_spm: Real scripts are placed on finer per-criterion bands (typically 4-5 levels, e.g. Excellent/Good/Satisfactory/Weak per criterion); a single 3-band 30-mark scale does not reflect how SPM examiners actually distribute marks

discrepancies.app_says: 'at least 200-250 words' (vague, dual figure)
discrepancies.real_spm: Word limit is a single stated figure (commonly 200 words for this task); a vague '200-250' is not how the paper states it, and the app gives no under-length penalty rule

discrepancies.app_says: No under-length or off-topic penalty stated
discrepancies.real_spm: Markers apply penalties/deductions for grossly under-length answers and for off-topic responses (content marks severely reduced); the rubric has no such mechanism

discrepancies.app_says: Generic 'genre conventions fully observed' with no task types listed
discrepancies.real_spm: Part 3 offers a choice of tasks (e.g. article, report, review, letter, story/description) each with its own conventions and format marks; rubric does not differentiate

discrepancies.app_says: Folded into one descriptor line
discrepancies.real_spm: Language is a full 10-mark criterion with sub-focus on range AND accuracy; the app's single line under-weights it and gives no guidance on error density thresholds

missing_in_app: Separate Content / Language / Organisation mark split (10+10+10)
Per-criterion band descriptors rather than one holistic band
Explicit under-length penalty rule
Off-topic / task-fulfilment deduction rule
Task-type-specific format/convention requirements (article, report, review, letter, story)
Guidance on error density and range (simple vs complex sentences) for the Language criterion
Register/audience awareness as a distinct descriptor
Word-count guidance as a single figure, not a range
critique.teacher_verdict: The rubric collapses a three-criterion, 10+10+10 SPM scheme into a single holistic A/B/C band, so it will not train students to secure marks criterion by criterion the way a real examiner does. The missing under-length and off-topic penalties are the most damaging gaps — students could submit a short or drifting essay and still be graded as if it were on-spec.

critique.real_required_length: 不少于 500 个汉字 for 命题作文 (SPM 华文 Kertas 1 作文部分; 应用文/短文另有规定)
critique.real_scheme: SPM 华文 Kertas 1 作文通常分为两部分：甲组应用文（如公函、私函、通告、启事等，约 20 分）和乙组命题作文（约 30 分）。命题作文评分一般按内容（约 12-15 分）和表达/语言（约 15-18 分）两大项，或按内容、结构、语言、标点/错别字分项给分；等级名称各州/年份略有差异，常见为‘优、良、及格、不及格’或 A/B/C/D/E 等级，而非 app 的‘优秀/良好/及格’三段式。字数不足通常按比例扣分或降档；离题会大幅降档。

discrepancies.item: 等级/band 名称与分数段
discrepancies.real_spm: SPM 华文作文评分通常按内容与表达分项给分，等级名称多为‘优/良/及格/不及格’或 A-E，且‘良好’跨 10 分过宽，不符合实际评分粒度。

discrepancies.app_says: 仅给三个 band 的描述性 descriptor，未拆分内容、语言、结构、格式的分数。
discrepancies.real_spm: 命题作文通常拆为内容（切题、充实、例证）、表达（语言通顺、词汇、语病）、结构/格式等分项，marker 按分项给分再合计。

discrepancies.app_says: 只写‘不少于 500 个汉字’，无扣分规则。
discrepancies.real_spm: 字数不足通常按不足比例扣分或降档；app 未体现 penalty。

discrepancies.app_says: ‘及格’band 含‘内容单薄或偏题’，但无明确离题降档规则。
discrepancies.real_spm: 离题通常大幅降档甚至不及格，marker 会先判切题性再给内容分。

discrepancies.app_says: 仅在 descriptor 提‘用词与标点准确’‘少量错别字’，无具体扣分。
discrepancies.real_spm: SPM 华文作文通常对错别字、标点错误有明确扣分上限或计入语言分。

discrepancies.app_says: 提‘文体格式规范/大致正确/不完整’，但未单列格式分。
discrepancies.real_spm: 命题作文虽以记叙/说明/议论文为主，格式要求相对应用文低，但 marker 仍会看结构完整；若题目要求特定文体，格式错误会影响表达分。

missing_in_app: 内容与表达（语言）分项给分及各自权重
字数不足的具体扣分/降档规则
离题/偏题的降档规则
错别字与标点错误的具体扣分上限
‘不及格’等级（app 最低为 1-15 及格，无不及格段）
marker 先判切题性再给内容分的流程
与甲组应用文（约 20 分）的整卷关系说明
critique.teacher_verdict: 这个 rubric 方向大致对（30 分、500 字、内容+语言+结构），但缺少 SPM 实际的分项给分、字数不足与离题降档、错别字扣分等关键 marker 操作，band 名称和分数段也不像 Lembaga Peperiksaan 的正式方案。用来练笔可以，但按它给分学生会不知道真实试卷上分从哪里来、哪里被扣。
